{{Short description|Special form of continuity}}
In [[mathematical analysis]], '''Dini continuity''' is a refinement of [[continuous function|continuity]]. Every Dini continuous function is continuous. Every [[Lipschitz continuous]] function and every [[Hölder condition|Hölder continuous]] function is Dini continuous.

==Definition==
Let <math>X</math> be a [[compact space|compact]] subset of a metric space (such as <math>\mathbb{R}^n</math>), and let <math>f:X\rightarrow X</math> be a function from <math>X</math> into itself.  The [[modulus of continuity]] of <math>f</math> is

:<math>\omega_f(t) = \sup_{d(x,y)\le t} d(f(x),f(y)). </math>

The function <math>f</math> is called '''Dini-continuous''' if

:<math>\int_0^1 \frac{\omega_f(t)}{t}\,dt < \infty.</math>

An equivalent condition is that, for any <math>\theta \in (0,1)</math>,

:<math>\sum_{i=1}^\infty \omega_f(\theta^i a) < \infty</math>

where <math>a</math> is the [[metric space#Bounded and totally bounded spaces|diameter]] of <math>X</math>.

==See also==
* [[Dini test]] — a condition similar to local Dini continuity implies convergence of a [[Fourier transform]].
* [[Kellogg's theorem]]
